s:
With reference to the Supreme Court's ruling in Rejanish K.V. v K. Deepa (October 2025), consider the following statements:
1. A five-judge Bench led by CJI B.R. Gavai held that serving judicial officers can be directly recruited as district judges.
2. The ruling overruled Satya Narain Singh (1984) and Dheeraj Mor v High Court of Delhi (2020).
3. Justice Sundresh held that an absolute bar on such recruitment violates Article 19(1)(g).
4. A candidate needs 7 years of advocacy and judicial service combined, with a uniform minimum age of 35 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: Justice Sundresh held that an absolute bar violates Article 14 (equality), not Article 19(1)(g).

s:
With reference to the Higher Judicial Services, consider the following statements:
1. Promotees make up about one-half of the cadre.
2. Under All India Judges Association (2002), 75% of posts are filled by promotion and 25% by direct recruitment.
3. The Supreme Court's May 2025 framework reduced the qualifying service from 5 years to 3 years.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Only two (2 and 3) are correct. 1 is wrong: promotees are about three-fourths of the cadre, though direct recruits dominate senior posts.

s:
With reference to the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA), consider the following statements:
1. The Chief Justice of India is its Patron-in-Chief.
2. The second senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is its Executive Chairman.
3. It is set up under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, giving effect to Article 21A of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: free legal aid flows from Article 39A (a Directive Principle), not Article 21A (right to education).

s:
Match List-I (Provision of the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025) with List-II (Supreme Court's interim decision):
List-I | List-II
a. 5 years of practising Islam to create a waqf | i. Religious practice continues under Sec 5(6), AMASR Act, 1958
b. Section 3C – Collector may declare waqf property as government property | ii. Stayed as 'totally unconstitutional'; title to be decided by the Waqf Tribunal
c. Mandatory registration of waqfs | iii. Stayed until a verification mechanism is framed
d. Waqfs that are protected monuments | iv. Upheld – required since 1923
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: The 5-year condition was stayed until a verification mechanism is framed; Section 3C was stayed and title left to the Waqf Tribunal (Sec 83); mandatory registration was upheld (required since 1923); religious practice continues at protected monuments under Sec 5(6) of the AMASR Act, 1958.

s:
With reference to the Supreme Court's interim ruling on the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. The Central Waqf Council may have at most 4 non-Muslims out of 22 members.
2. A State Waqf Board may have at most 5 non-Muslims out of 11 members.
3. The Act's validity was upheld overall while arbitrary provisions were stayed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: a State Waqf Board may have at most 3 non-Muslims of 11, and its CEO should preferably be a Muslim.

s:
With reference to minority schools and the RTE Act, consider the following statements:
1. In Pramati (2014) a five-judge Bench exempted both aided and unaided minority schools from the RTE Act.
2. In Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan (2012) the Supreme Court exempted all aided schools from the RTE Act.
3. In September 2025 Justices Dipankar Datta and Manmohan referred Pramati to a larger Bench, holding that Article 21A and Article 30(1) must co-exist.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 3) are correct. 2 is wrong: the 2012 Rajasthan case upheld the RTE Act and exempted only unaided minority schools.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Under Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act, 2009, private unaided schools must reserve 25% of entry-level seats for disadvantaged groups, with the State reimbursing them.
Reason (R): Article 30(1) gives only religious minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true: Section 12(1)(c) mandates 25% of entry-level seats with State reimbursement. R is false: Article 30(1) covers all minorities, religious and linguistic.

s:
Match List-I (Case) with List-II (Holding on DNA evidence):
List-I | List-II
a. Anil v Maharashtra (2014) | i. Rejected – sample lay in the Malkhana for 2 months
b. Manoj v Madhya Pradesh (2022) | ii. Rejected – sample collected from an open area
c. Rahul v Delhi (2022) | iii. Reliable only with quality control
d. Kattavellai @ Devakar v Tamil Nadu | iv. Sample to reach the FSL within 48 hours; Chain of Custody Register
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Anil (2014): DNA reliable only with quality control; Manoj (2022): rejected, sample from an open area; Rahul (2022): rejected, sample in the Malkhana for 2 months; Kattavellai: directions – FSL within 48 hours, documented packaging, Chain of Custody Register.

s:
With reference to DNA evidence as dealt with in Kattavellai @ Devakar v State of Tamil Nadu, consider the following statements:
1. DNA evidence is opinion evidence that needs corroboration.
2. Section 45 of the Evidence Act (expert opinion) corresponds to Section 57 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.
3. The Court directed that a Chain of Custody Register be maintained for samples.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Section 45 of the Evidence Act corresponds to Section 39 of the BSA, 2023.

s:
With reference to criminal defamation in India, consider the following statements:
1. Under Sections 499 and 500 IPC it is punishable with imprisonment up to 2 years, fine or both.
2. In Subramanian Swamy v Union of India (2016) the Supreme Court struck it down as violating Article 19(1)(a).
3. In September 2025 Justice M.M. Sundresh flagged its misuse in the Foundation for Independent Journalism case.
4. The United Kingdom has abolished criminal defamation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: Subramanian Swamy (2016) upheld criminal defamation, treating reputation as part of Article 21.

s:
With reference to the Section 152 BNS proceedings against journalists of The Wire, consider the following statements:
1. Assam Police summoned Siddharth Varadarajan and Karan Thapar over their coverage of Operation Sindoor.
2. Section 152 BNS is seen as a rebranded version of Section 153A IPC.
3. The summons lacked the FIR date, the offence details and a copy of the FIR.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 3) are correct. 2 is wrong: Section 152 BNS is seen as a rebranded Section 124A IPC (sedition), in abeyance since 2022.

s:
Match List-I (High Court) with List-II (2025 ruling):
List-I | List-II
a. Andhra Pradesh High Court | i. Upheld the Sahyog Portal as 'an instrument of public good'
b. Karnataka High Court | ii. SC status ceases immediately on conversion to Christianity
c. Delhi High Court | iii. Cultivating any cannabis plant is illegal even without flowering tops
d. Kerala High Court | iv. Protected the personality rights of Aishwarya Rai Bachchan and others against AI deepfakes
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: AP HC (Justice N. Harinath): SC status ceases on conversion to Christianity; Karnataka HC dismissed X Corp's plea and upheld the Sahyog Portal; Delhi HC protected Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, Abhishek Bachchan and Karan Johar; Kerala HC (4 Nov 2025) on cannabis cultivation.

s:
Match List-I (Personality-rights case) with List-II (Holding):
List-I | List-II
a. R. Rajagopal v Tamil Nadu (1994) | i. AI voice cloning restrained
b. DM Entertainment v Baby Gift House (2010) | ii. Daler Mehndi dolls restrained
c. Anil Kapoor (Delhi HC, 2023) | iii. Right to control one's identity under Article 21
d. Arijit Singh (Bombay HC, 2024) | iv. 'jhakaas' protected
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: R. Rajagopal – right to control one's identity (Art 21); DM Entertainment – Daler Mehndi dolls; Anil Kapoor – 'jhakaas'; Arijit Singh – AI voice cloning.

s:
Consider the following statements on the internet and privacy:
1. In Faheema Shirin v Kerala (2019) the Kerala High Court held internet access to be part of Article 21.
2. In Anuradha Bhasin v Union of India (2020) the Supreme Court ruled against indefinite internet shutdowns under Article 19.
3. The United Nations declared internet access a human right in 2012.
4. Puttaswamy (2017) held privacy to be a fundamental right under Article 21.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the UN declared internet access a human right in 2016.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): In the Kerala hijab row, the freedom of religion under Article 25 is subject to public order, morality and health.
Reason (R): A school's institutional autonomy is linked with Article 19(1)(g).
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: Article 25 is subject to public order, morality and health, and school autonomy is traced to Article 19(1)(g). But R does not explain A – the limits on Article 25 come from Article 25 itself; courts balance the two by the proportionality test.

s:
With reference to cannabis under the NDPS Act, 1985, consider the following statements:
1. Charas means the resin of cannabis, including hashish oil.
2. Ganja means the leaves of the cannabis plant.
3. Bhang is not a narcotic under the NDPS Act and is left to the States.
4. Section 8(b) lets the Government permit cultivation for industrial, horticultural, medical or scientific use.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: ganja is the flowering/fruiting tops (bhang is leaves). 4 is wrong: Section 8(b) bans cultivation without approval; Section 14 lets the Government permit it.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Uttarakhand issued India's first industrial-hemp licences in 2018.
2. India's first medical cannabis clinic opened in Hyderabad in 2020.
3. The UN Commission on Narcotic Drugs (1946), the main policy body on global drug control, is based at Geneva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the first medical cannabis clinic was in Bengaluru (2020). 3 is wrong: the UN CND is based at Vienna.

s:
With reference to the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. It was introduced in the Lok Sabha by the Union Home Minister and amends Article 75, along with Articles 164 and 239AA.
2. It applies to a Minister held in custody for 30 consecutive days on charges punishable with at least 7 years.
3. A Minister removed under it is permanently disqualified from re-appointment.
4. It covers the Prime Minister and Chief Ministers as well as Union and State Ministers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the charges must be punishable with at least 5 years. 3 is wrong: there is no permanent disqualification – re-appointment is possible after release.

s:
With reference to the Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) on the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. It has 31 members – 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.
2. A JPC is a standing committee of Parliament.
3. By July 2026 the Bill was left out of the Monsoon Session agenda, with the JPC's deadline extended.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 3) are correct. 2 is wrong: a JPC is an ad hoc body, not a standing committee.

s:
Match List-I (Case / Provision) with List-II (Point):
List-I (Case / Provision) | List-II (Point)
a. Manoj Narula v UoI (2014) | i. Parliamentary accountability
b. Ram Jawaya Kapur v Punjab (1955) | ii. Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers
c. S.R. Bommai (1994) | iii. PM's advice on appointing Ministers binding unless the person is constitutionally disqualified
d. Articles 75(3) and 164(2) | iv. Floor test
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Manoj Narula – PM's advice binding unless constitutionally disqualified; Ram Jawaya Kapur – parliamentary accountability; S.R. Bommai – floor test; Arts 75(3)/164(2) – collective responsibility (75(1)/164(1) deal with appointment).

s:
With reference to Chandigarh, consider the following statements:
1. If added to Article 240, Chandigarh would get an independent Administrator/Lt-Governor and the President could make regulations for it.
2. It became a Union Territory and the joint capital under the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966.
3. Since 1984 the Governor of Haryana has been its Administrator.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: since 1984 the Governor of Punjab (not Haryana) has been the Administrator of Chandigarh.

s:
With reference to the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. It received assent on 22 August 2025 and bans online money games.
2. Online social games are banned along with online money games.
3. Offences under it are cognisable and non-bailable.
4. Offering money games is punishable with up to 3 years and ₹1 crore, while players are not penalised.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Act promotes e-sports and online social games (casual/educational, no betting); only money games are banned.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Betting and gambling are subjects in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule.
Reason (R): The challenge to the Online Gaming Act, 2025 on the skill-versus-chance distinction invokes Article 19(1)(g).
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: betting and gambling are in the State List (Entries 34 and 62). R is true: the skill-vs-chance challenge invokes the freedom of trade under Article 19(1)(g).

s:
With reference to the IIM (Amendment) Bill, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. It provides for the 22nd IIM at Guwahati, Assam.
2. It amends the Indian Institutes of Management Act, 2017.
3. The first IIM was set up in 1961.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: the 22nd IIM is at Guwahati, the Bill amends the IIM Act, 2017, and the first IIM came in 1961.

s:
With reference to the Draft Registration Bill, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. It was released by the Ministry of Law and Justice.
2. It replaces the Registration Act, 1908.
3. Under Section 29, registration may be denied if the person has no Aadhaar.
4. Land and property disputes make up over two-thirds of civil cases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: the draft is from the Ministry of Rural Development. 3 is wrong: Section 29(4) says registration cannot be denied for lack of Aadhaar.

s:
With reference to the Election Commission of India, consider the following statements:
1. Under the 2023 law, its members are selected by a committee chaired by the Prime Minister.
2. A Commissioner holds office for 6 years or until the age of 65.
3. It advises the President on the disqualification of Members of Parliament under Article 102.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the ECI's opinion on disqualification of MPs is given under Article 103 (Article 192 for MLAs).

s:
With reference to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, consider the following statements:
1. On 10 July 2025 the Supreme Court stayed the Bihar SIR.
2. The Court directed the ECI to accept Aadhaar as the 12th valid document, as proof of identity but not of citizenship.
3. The pan-India SIR was announced on 27 October 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the Court did not stay the Bihar SIR; it ordered publication of the draft roll.

s:
Match List-I (Case / Provision) with List-II (Point):
List-I (Case / Provision) | List-II (Point)
a. Lal Babu Hussain (1995) | i. Manifesto promises are not a 'corrupt practice' under Section 123, RPA
b. Mohinder Singh Gill (1978) | ii. Only citizens can be registered as electors
c. Section 16, RPA 1950 | iii. Article 324 powers are plenary but within limits
d. S. Subramaniam Balaji v TN (2013) | iv. Burden of proving citizenship lies on new registrants
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Lal Babu Hussain – burden on new registrants; Mohinder Singh Gill – Art 324 plenary within limits; Sec 16 RPA 1950 – only citizens as electors; Subramaniam Balaji – manifesto promises not a corrupt practice.

s:
With reference to electoral-roll integrity, consider the following statements:
1. After fraudulent Form-7 applications (objections to inclusion/deletion) in Aland, the ECI made Aadhaar-linked mobile verification mandatory on ECINet.
2. ECINET was announced on 4 May 2025 and first used in the 19 June 2025 bypolls.
3. In those bypolls, turnout was uploaded by the Returning Officers after counting.
4. Before the 2019 elections the EC told Chief Electoral Officers to continue uploading machine-readable rolls.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: presiding officers uploaded turnout before leaving the polling station. 4 is wrong: the EC told CEOs to stop uploading machine-readable rolls.

s:
With reference to the Vice-Presidential election of September 2025, consider the following statements:
1. C.P. Radhakrishnan (NDA) defeated B. Sudershan Reddy, the joint opposition candidate.
2. The Returning Officer was the Secretary General of the Lok Sabha.
3. The minimum age to be Vice-President is 30 years.
4. The electoral college has elected and nominated members of both Houses; State MLAs do not vote.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Returning Officer was P.C. Mody, Secretary General of the Rajya Sabha. 3 is wrong: the minimum age is 35.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The National Emergency of 25 June 1975 was proclaimed on the ground of 'internal disturbance'.
Reason (R): The 44th Amendment (1978) replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' in Article 352.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true, but R does not explain A: the 1975 proclamation used 'internal disturbance', which the 44th Amendment replaced only later, in 1978.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Union Cabinet resolved to observe 25 June as 'Samvidhan Hatya Diwas'.
2. The 1975 Emergency ended on 21 March 1977.
3. The 42nd Amendment, the 'Mini-Constitution', added 'Socialist' and 'Secular' to the Preamble.
4. A Financial Emergency is proclaimed under Article 356.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: a Financial Emergency is under Article 360; Article 356 is President's Rule.

s:
With reference to the UPSC, consider the following statements:
1. It entered its centenary year on 1 October 2025.
2. The Public Service Commission was set up in October 1926 with Sir Ross Barker as its first chairman.
3. The Federal Public Service Commission came into being in 1950.
4. PRATIBHA Setu links interview-stage candidates who are not finally selected with jobs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Federal Public Service Commission came in 1935 (Government of India Act); the 1924 Lee Commission had recommended the commission.

s:
Match List-I (e-Courts Project) with List-II (Detail):
List-I | List-II
a. Phase I (2010–2015) | i. Courts computerised
b. Phase II (2015–2023) | ii. e-filing, e-payment, NJDG, virtual courts
c. Phase III (2023–2027) | iii. Outlay of ₹7,210 crore
d. Origin | iv. National Policy and Action Plan for ICT in Indian Judiciary, 2005
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Phase I computerised courts; Phase II brought e-filing, e-payment, NJDG and virtual courts; Phase III has ₹7,210 crore; the project grew out of the SC e-Committee's 2005 National Policy and Action Plan.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. According to the India Justice Report 2025, women are 3.1% of High Court judges and 14% of Supreme Court judges.
2. Under Article 312, Parliament can create an All-India Judicial Service.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 2 is correct. 1 reverses the figures: women are 14% of High Court judges and 3.1% of Supreme Court judges.

s:
With reference to Left-Wing Extremism (LWE), consider the following statements:
1. Former Politburo member Mallojula Venugopal Rao surrendered, calling Chinese and Russian models irrelevant.
2. LWE-affected districts have fallen from 90+ to 11.
3. The Supreme Court banned Salwa Judum in 2015.
4. FARC, cited as a global parallel, operated in Peru.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Salwa Judum was banned in 2011. 4 is wrong: FARC is from Colombia (Shining Path is from Peru).

s:
With reference to the Census, consider the following statements:
1. Census 2027 comes after a 6-year delay and is fully digital.
2. Under Census 2027, geotagging is done during Population Enumeration.
3. As per Census 2011, Jains recorded the lowest decadal growth (5.4%) in 2001–11.
4. As per Census 2011, Hindus were 79.8% of the population.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: geotagging is done during the Houselisting Operations, not Population Enumeration.

s:
Under Andhra Pradesh's SC sub-categorisation Ordinance, match List-I (Group) with List-II (Detail):
List-I (Group) | List-II (Detail)
a. Group I | i. 12 castes – 1%
b. Group II | ii. 29 castes – 7.5%
c. Group III | iii. 18 castes – 6.5%
d. Unit of application | iv. Whole State as one unit on the 2011 census
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: The 59 SC communities are in three groups: Group I – 12 castes, 1%; Group II – 18 castes, 6.5%; Group III – 29 castes, 7.5% (total 15%); the State is one unit on the 2011 census.

s:
With reference to the Ladakh protests of September 2025, consider the following statements:
1. They were led by the Leh Apex Body and the Kargil Democratic Alliance.
2. Their demands included statehood and the Sixth Schedule.
3. Under the May 2025 measures, 85% of jobs were reserved for locals.
4. The May 2025 measures gave 33% reservation to women in the LAHDC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the May 2025 measures reserved 95% of jobs for locals.

s:
With reference to the creation of States, consider the following statements:
1. Sikkim was admitted as a State under Article 2 in 1975.
2. Article 3 empowers Parliament to form new States and alter their area, boundaries and names.
3. Goa was acquired in 1975 and Sikkim in 1961.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 reverses the years: Goa was acquired in 1961 and Sikkim in 1975.

s:
With reference to the Uniform Civil Code, consider the following statements:
1. Article 44 (UCC) is a Directive Principle of State Policy.
2. Under the amended Uttarakhand UCC Rules, the Registrar cannot inform the parents of live-in registrants below 18.
3. Non-registration or a false declaration is punishable with 3 months or ₹25,000.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 3) are correct. 2 is wrong: the age is 21 – the Registrar cannot inform the parents of live-in registrants below 21.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I | List-II
a. Manki (Kolhan system) | i. 'Sons of the Soil' (1978)
b. Wilkinson's Rules | ii. Coined the term 'provincial citizenship'
c. Alok Ranjan | iii. Heads 8–15 villages, appellate authority
d. Myron Weiner | iv. Customs, not formal law (Mora Ho, Patna HC 2000)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: The Manki heads 8–15 villages (a Munda heads one); Mora Ho (2000) held Wilkinson's Rules to be customs; Alok Ranjan coined 'provincial citizenship'; Myron Weiner wrote 'Sons of the Soil' (1978).

s:
Match List-I (Labour Code) with List-II (Number of Central laws merged):
List-I (Labour Code) | List-II (Laws merged)
a. Code on Wages, 2019 | i. 3
b. Code on Social Security, 2020 | ii. 9
c. Industrial Relations Code, 2020 | iii. 4
d. OSH Code, 2020 | iv. 13
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Code on Wages – 4 laws; Social Security – 9; Industrial Relations – 3 (Industrial Disputes Act 1947, Trade Unions Act 1926, Standing Orders); OSH – 13; 29 in all.

s:
Match List-I (Labour Code) with List-II (Feature):
List-I (Labour Code) | List-II (Feature)
a. Code on Wages, 2019 | i. Appointment letters and annual free health check mandatory
b. Code on Social Security, 2020 | ii. National Floor Wage
c. Industrial Relations Code, 2020 | iii. Layoff permission threshold raised from 100 to 300 workers
d. OSH Code, 2020 | iv. First legal definition of gig and platform workers
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Wages – National Floor Wage; Social Security – gig and platform workers defined; IR – layoff threshold 100 → 300 (not 500); OSH – appointment letters and free annual health check.

s:
With reference to the Labour Codes, consider the following statements:
1. Under the Code on Wages, overtime is paid at twice the normal rate.
2. Under the Code on Wages, total deductions from wages are capped at 50%.
3. Under the Code on Social Security, aggregators pay 1–2% of turnover for gig and platform workers.
4. Fixed-term employees become eligible for gratuity only after 5 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: under the Code on Social Security, fixed-term employees get gratuity after 1 year.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. From 21 November 2025, four Labour Codes replaced 29 Central labour laws.
2. Labour is a subject in the Union List.
3. Under the OSH Code, a factory using power needs a licence from 20 workers (earlier 10).
4. The Industrial Relations Code raised the layoff permission threshold from 100 to 500 workers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: labour is in the Concurrent List (Entries 22–24, 35). 4 is wrong: the threshold was raised to 300, not 500.

s:
Arrange the following events of 2025 in chronological order:
1. Presidential Reference under Article 143(1) on Articles 200 and 201
2. Judgment of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and R. Mahadevan in the Tamil Nadu Governor case
3. Five-judge Bench opinion rejecting 'deemed assent'
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: The TN Governor judgment (Pardiwala, Mahadevan) came on 8 April 2025; the Presidential Reference on Arts 200 and 201 in May 2025; the five-judge opinion (CJI Gavai) in November 2025.

s:
With reference to the Supreme Court's November 2025 opinion on the Presidential Reference, consider the following statements:
1. It was given by a five-judge Bench led by CJI B.R. Gavai.
2. It accepted the idea of 'deemed assent' when a Governor sits on a Bill.
3. It held that a limited mandamus is possible for prolonged, unexplained inaction.
4. The April 2025 judgment it reviewed had set the first judicially enforceable timelines on Governors and the President.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Only three (1, 3 and 4) are correct. 2 is wrong: the Bench rejected deemed assent and court-imposed timelines.

s:
With reference to Article 200, consider the following statements:
1. The Governor may reserve a Bill for the consideration of the Supreme Court.
2. Article 200 requires the Governor to act on a Bill within three months.
3. The Governor cannot return a Money Bill for reconsideration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: a Bill may be reserved for the President, not the Supreme Court. 2 is wrong: Article 200 says only 'as soon as possible'.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The Governor's decision on a matter within his discretion cannot be questioned in a court.
Reason (R): Article 163(2) makes the Governor's decision on whether a matter is within his discretion final.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

With reference to the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Rules, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. They were notified on 14 November 2025.
2. The Data Protection Board of India is a subordinate office of the Ministry of Home Affairs.
3. A person can name a digital nominee to act after death or incapacity.
4. A Data Fiduciary is the individual whose data is processed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Board is a subordinate office of MeitY. 4 is wrong: the individual is the Data Principal; the Data Fiduciary decides the purpose and means of processing.

Assertion (A): The DPDP framework amended Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act, removing the public-interest override for personal information.
Reason (R): The draft data protection Bill of 2018 was prepared by the Justice A.P. Shah Committee.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true: Section 8(1)(j) was amended to drop the public-interest override. R is false: the 2018 draft was prepared by the Srikrishna Committee.

With reference to the Immigration and Foreigners Order, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. It replaced the Foreigners (Tribunal) Order, 1964.
2. Foreigners Tribunals exist in Assam and West Bengal.
3. It gave a clear legal basis for detention for the first time.
4. After the IMDT Act, 1983 was struck down in 2005, the 11 IMDTs became Foreigners Tribunals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: Foreigners Tribunals exist only in Assam.

Consider the following statements:
1. The Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) Order, 2025 exempts Sri Lankan Tamils who sheltered in India on or before 9 January 2015.
2. The Exemption Order confers citizenship on those it covers.
3. The CAA 2019 covers six minorities who entered India before 31 December 2014.
4. India is a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention but not to the 1967 Protocol.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Exemption Order does not confer citizenship. 4 is wrong: India has signed neither the 1951 Convention nor the 1967 Protocol.
